supporting_observations.claim: Multiple connections from WS-LMARTINS-01 to the explicit proxy at 10.40.20.30:8080 appear during the review window. The recorded sessions include 13:30:58, 13:40:51, 13:43:21, 13:45:21, 13:50:28, 13:55:32, 14:00:10, 14:05:36, and 14:10:35 UTC; the provided records do not show a uniform five-minute interval.
The 14:10:35 session was an HTTPS CONNECT tunnel to updates.pixelforge-suite.com, and the connection was associated with the approved PixelForge updater executable, pfupdater.exe.

The confirmed 14:10:35 destination and executable match the inventory's approved PixelForge update service and updater, which checks for updates about every five minutes. This supports a benign explanation for at least that session, but does not identify the earlier sessions.
WS-LMARTINS-01 made SMB connections to FILE-NWD-01 at 13:55:37 and 14:03:22 UTC. The corresponding file-server logon records identify ANONYMOUS LOGON using NTLM.

At 14:11:03 UTC, DC-NWD-01 connected to WS-LMARTINS-01 on RPC endpoint mapper port 135. A WmiPrvSE.exe process running as SYSTEM ended at 14:11:23, but these records do not establish that the connection caused the process to run or what it did.

The RPC source is notable because the provided environment context says remote administration is only performed from WS-SOKAFOR-01; the evidence does not establish whether this DC-to-workstation RPC connection was authorized for another purpose.

known_telemetry_limitations: For the earlier proxy-bound sessions, the provided records show connections to the proxy but do not identify the requested destination or originating process. The detailed CONNECT and process attribution are available for the 14:10:35 session only (T056-00043, T056-00082, T056-00108, T056-00112, T056-00128, T056-00148, T056-00168, T056-00179, T056-00192, T056-00193, T056-00195).
The supplied records do not include decrypted HTTPS content or other evidence of what was transferred in the tunnels (T056-00192, T056-00194, T056-00195).

The SMB and RPC records show connections and logon/process events, but do not provide the accessed share or file, the RPC/WMI operation, or evidence of resulting changes (T056-00151, T056-00152, T056-00154, T056-00172, T056-00174, T056-00176, T056-00200, T056-00201, T056-00202, T056-00203).
claims_not_established: Whether the proxy sessions before 14:10:35 were also PixelForge updater checks, or involved another destination or process.
Whether the SMB connections accessed data or performed an action beyond establishing a session.
Whether the DC-to-workstation RPC connection was authorized, what operation it performed, or whether it resulted in remote execution.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve complete proxy CONNECT records for all WS-LMARTINS-01 sessions in the review window, including destination, user agent, byte counts, and any available TLS certificate or SNI details.
Correlate each proxy session with endpoint process telemetry, including process creation details, executable hash and signature, and network events.
Review FILE-NWD-01 SMB share-access and file-access auditing for the 13:55:37 and 14:03:22 connections.
Review DC-NWD-01 and WS-LMARTINS-01 RPC/WMI and remote-management logs around 14:11 UTC, and determine whether the activity was authorized.
Check change, patching, and endpoint-management records for an explanation of the observed SMB and RPC activity.
